verdict.rationale: Phoenix's docs say it supports deterministic code-based evaluators, including custom heuristics, and offer Python and TypeScript SDKs with full control over evaluation logic. Those evaluators can run on traces, experiment results, or datasets. However, the evidence only states this at a high level and never shows how a user authors a custom scorer function or defines custom aggregate metrics. missing for 10: documented API or interface for defining custom scorer functions, custom aggregate metric definitions, code examples, independent or hands-on corroboration of custom code scorers.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can write custom code-based scorers and metrics for my evaluations

citations.quote: Phoenix supports both deterministic code-based evaluators (exact match, regex, custom heuristics) and LLM-as-a-judge evaluators
Python and TypeScript SDKs for running evaluations against Phoenix traces, datasets, or any data source. Full control over evaluation logic, judge models, and pipelines.
You can score traces & spans with LLM-based evaluators, code-based checks, or human labels
Dataset Evaluators serve as test cases that automatically score outputs when running experiments
